      • removeNjamsFromSharedReceiver

        public static boolean removeNjamsFromSharedReceiver​(ShareableReceiver<?> receiver,
                                                    Njams njams)
        Removes the given Njams instance from the given shared receiver and, if that was the last user, evicts the receiver from the shared-receiver cache — both steps performed atomically under this factory's shared-receiver lock, so that a later Njams concurrently calling getReceiver(Njams) for the same receiver type can never observe the receiver as still cached after it has genuinely stopped. Without this atomicity, ShareableReceiver.removeNjams(Njams) reporting "last user" and the cache eviction would be two separate, un-synchronized steps, leaving a window in which a concurrently constructing Njams is handed the doomed instance right before it is evicted (SDK-375 final-review finding).

        A stopped AbstractReceiver cannot be reconnected: its connectBegun flag is a one-shot, final field that AbstractReceiver.beginConnect() never resets, and once shouldShutdown is set its reconnect loop permanently refuses to run. Evicting the dead instance — rather than attempting to reset and reuse it — is therefore the only way a later Njams sharing the same receiver type can connect at all.

        This method is public because Njams, which needs to call it, lives in a different package; the communication layer as a whole remains internal SDK infrastructure and not public API (see the project's API design rules).

        Parameters:
        receiver - the shared receiver instance the given njams is being removed from.
        njams - the Njams instance to remove.
        Returns:
        true if this was the last user, i.e., the receiver has genuinely stopped and been evicted; false if other instances still use it.
        Since:
        6.1.0

      • clearSharedReceiversForTesting

        public static void clearSharedReceiversForTesting()
        Test-support only: unconditionally clears the entire shared-receiver cache, regardless of whether any cached receiver has genuinely stopped. Production code must never call this.

        It exists so lifecycle tests in a different package (e.g. a SharedReceiverRestartSpecTest under com.im.njams.sdk.communication.lifecycle) can reset this static state unconditionally in their teardown, without depending on every test's Njams.stop() call having actually run — a test whose Njams.start() unexpectedly returns false would otherwise skip stop() and leave a shut-down shared receiver cached, poisoning every later shared-receiver test in the same JVM (SDK-375 final-review finding on test static-state fragility). public only because that test lives in a different package (com.im.njams.sdk.communication.lifecycle); kept to this single, narrow method rather than exposing the cache itself.

      • validateSenderConfiguration

        public void validateSenderConfiguration()
        Checks the settings for creating a sender, without creating one: the communication type must be configured, and at least one implementation must be registered for it. Whether such an implementation is applicable in this environment is only found out when the sender is created.
        Throws:
        IllegalStateException - if the communication type is not configured, or no sender implementation is registered for it.
